title: Descent of canonical source-open loci from scheme-target tests
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and morphisms and $2$-fibre products of fibred groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. An open subspace is a subfunctor whose scheme pullbacks are open subschemes [def-a1-space-open-subspace]; an open substack is a strictly full substack with this same scheme-pullback condition [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant predicate on morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume: (i) $P$ is stable under arbitrary base change; (ii) $P$ is fppf local on the target, meaning that for every surjective flat locally finitely presented map $T^{\prime}\to T$, a map $E\to T$ has $P$ if and only if $E\times_TT^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ has $P$; (iii) $P$ is etale local on the source, meaning that precomposition by an etale map preserves $P$ and a jointly surjective etale family detects $P$. Here flatness, local finite presentation and etaleness are tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism]; joint surjectivity is surjectivity on field-valued point classes. Suppose that for every locally finite type map $g:E\to T$ with $E$ an algebraic space and $T$ a scheme there is a largest open subspace $W_g\subseteq E$ on which $g$ has $P$, and that for every scheme map $T'\to T$ one has $W_{g_{T'}}=W_g\times_TT'$. Local finite type means [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] on etale charts. Extend $P$ to representable maps of algebraic stacks by requiring it on every scheme base change; representable means that all those base changes are algebraic spaces. Then every locally finite type map $f:A\to\mathcal Y$ from an algebraic space to an algebraic stack has a largest open subspace $W_f\subseteq A$ on which $f$ has $P$. For every representable morphism $b:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ of algebraic stacks, put $A_b=A\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ and $f_b:A_b\to\mathcal Z$. The space $A_b$ is algebraic and $W_{f_b}=W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ as open subspaces of $A_b$. In particular this equality holds when $\mathcal Z$ is any scheme. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), source-open descent construction and (A),(B), in the scheme-target test formulation with Q = locally of finite type and R = all morphisms; the preliminary extension from scheme targets to space targets is etale descent of the same canonical opens.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $v:V\to\mathcal Y$. Since $\mathcal Y$ has representable diagonal, the diagonal criterion makes $f:A\to\mathcal Y$ representable. Put $U=A\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, $B=V\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, and $R=U\times_AU\simeq A\times_{\mathcal Y}B$. The diagonal criterion and representable pullback over a space make these algebraic spaces. The chartwise calculus gives smooth surjections $U\to A$ and $B\to V$ and makes $g:U\to V$ locally of finite type. For the displayed comparison, an object of $U\times_AU$ consists of one $A$ object, two $V$ objects and isomorphisms from their images to that $A$ object's image. Composing one isomorphism with the inverse of the other gives the $B$ coordinate; retaining one comparison gives the $A\times_{\mathcal Y}B$ coordinate. Inserting the composite reverses this operation, including on arrows. Let $O=W_g\subseteq U$, provided by the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (A),(B); scheme refinements of the overlap implement the scheme-target hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $b_1,b_2:B\to V$ be the projections. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $D\to B$. Both maps $D\to V$ are scheme maps. The pullbacks of $g$ along them identify with the same map $h:A\times_{\mathcal Y}D\to D$; the comparison uses the isomorphism between the two $\mathcal Y$ images in the definition of $B$. It is locally of finite type by base change. Thus the assumed scheme-base-change formula identifies both inverse images of $O$ in $A\times_{\mathcal Y}D$ with $W_h$. The map $A\times_{\mathcal Y}D\to R$ is surjective etale, so the two inverse images of $O$ in $R$ agree. Explicitly, after a scheme test of $R$, pull back this etale cover; the two open subfunctors agree on the resulting covering. Membership in either open subfunctor is etale local, since open subspaces are sheaves by their algebraic-space definition. Hence the equality holds before the cover. No largest locus over the space target $B$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (A),(B); scheme refinements of the overlap implement the scheme-target hypothesis.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $e:H\to U$. Then $q:H\to A$ is smooth surjective, and $O_H=e^{-1}O$ is an open subscheme. Pulling the equality of step 2 to $H\times_AH$ makes $O_H$ invariant. Invariant-open descent for the smooth scheme atlas $q$ gives an open substack $W\subseteq A$ with $H\times_AW=O_H$. This is an open subspace: $W\to A$ is representable by schemes, and representable pullback over the algebraic space $A$ makes $W\simeq W\times_AA$ an algebraic space. Its pullback to $U$ equals $O$, since the two opens agree on $H$ and equality of open subfunctors is detected etale locally as in step 2.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (A),(B); scheme refinements of the overlap implement the scheme-target hypothesis.

proof.text: For each scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, set $C=T\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. It is a space by the diagonal criterion, and $C\to T$ is smooth surjective, hence flat and locally finitely presented. The pullback of $W_T:=W\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T$ along this fppf map is $O\times_VC\to C$. Explicitly, $W_T\times_TC\simeq(W\times_{\mathcal Y}V)\times_VC$. Since $O\to V$ has $P$, base-change stability of $P$ and its assumed fppf target locality give $P(W_T\to T)$. Thus $W\to\mathcal Y$ has extended $P$. If $J\subseteq A$ is any open on which $f$ has extended $P$, its scheme base change $J\times_{\mathcal Y}V\to V$ has $P$, so $J\times_{\mathcal Y}V\subseteq O$ by maximality of $O$. Pullback to $H$ gives $J\times_AH\subseteq O_H$. The factorization criterion in invariant-open descent yields $J\subseteq W$. Write $W_f=W$.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (A),(B); scheme refinements of the overlap implement the scheme-target hypothesis.

proof.text: We prove the chart identity $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}T=W_{f_T}$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Form $C=T\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ and choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $D\to C$. Let $E=A\times_{\mathcal Y}D$ and $A_T=A\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. Both $D\to V$ and $D\to T$ are scheme maps. Applied to $g:U\to V$ and $f_T:A_T\to T$, the assumed formula identifies the inverse images of $O$ and $W_{f_T}$ in $E$ with the same open $W_{E\to D}$. These maps are locally of finite type by base change. Since $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}V=O$, the inverse image of $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ in $E$ is also this open. The map $E\to A_T$ is smooth surjective. Refine it by a surjective etale scheme atlas $K\to E$; then $K\to A_T$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas. The two opens of $A_T$ have equal pullbacks to $K$, so the injectivity of invariant-open descent proves the chart identity. There is no flatness assumption on $T\to\mathcal Y$.

source.place: Tag 06M3 (lemma-local-source), proof of (A),(B); scheme refinements of the overlap implement the scheme-target hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $b:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ be representable. Representable pullback over $A$ makes $A_b=A\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ a space; $f_b$ is representable and locally of finite type by base change. Apply steps 1--4 to $f_b$ to obtain its largest open $W_{f_b}$. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $T\to\mathcal Z$. By step 5 for $f$ and for $f_b$, the two opens $W_f\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ and $W_{f_b}$ have the same inverse image in $A_b\times_{\mathcal Z}T$: both equal $W_{A_b\times_{\mathcal Z}T\to T}$. Refining $A_b\times_{\mathcal Z}T\to A_b$ by an etale scheme atlas gives a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $A_b$, on which these opens agree. Invariant-open descent therefore gives their equality on $A_b$. A scheme $\mathcal Z$ is included, since every scheme map to $\mathcal Y$ is representable by the diagonal criterion. Every cover used above is an arbitrary smooth or etale atlas; no quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis entered.
